findings.title: The exact-token release primitive is stale-ACK and stale-token safe

evidence.observation: The transaction locks by result id, returns an existing result-id/token release receipt idempotently, then requires processing/possibly_dispatched/exact claim token before an exact update or delete.
The frozen fixture covers deleted/restored disposition, idempotent replay, wrong token/state, stale ACK and inter-session race.

findings.condition: Do not weaken exact result-id/token predicates or treat the local privileged dblink race as a NOSUPERUSER operating-race proof.

findings.title: Frozen source could downgrade a prior returned response into a release-authorizing final credential rejection

evidence.observation: The report correctly traces the frozen per-model providerResponseReceived reset and final true flag.
Current code monotonically records nonCredentialOutcomeObserved. A later credential rejection throws true only if none was observed; otherwise it breaks and returns GeminiOcrError(...,false).

findings.currentImplementation: The unsafe response-model to credential-model sequence now stops at the credential-model. It does not call the third model or rotate to another credential, and the durable layer therefore takes markIndeterminate rather than exact release.
findings.condition: Preserve the monotonic operation history. No later model or credential may turn a mixed history back into definitiveCredentialRejection=true.
verification: The current helper regression observes exactly response-model and credential-model, definitiveCredentialRejection=false, and no third-model or next-credential call.
The current helper and test hashes match the integrated verification receipt.

Tests preserve successful pure credential rotation, reject mixed model history, and keep credential-then-transport uncertainty non-definitive.

findings.currentImplementation: accepted as the minimum safe structure
findings.condition: If product policy later wants to continue fallback after mixed history, the two-predicate design or an equivalent explicit state model becomes necessary. The current policy intentionally stops instead.
verification: Keep pure credential-only fallback coverage.
Keep the assertion that neither another model nor another credential is dispatched after the mixed stop.

amendFrozen106.invalidStateBehavior: A pre-seal allowlist assertion could atomically abort a brand-new 106 install before a valid seal. It cannot remediate a database where 106 is already applied, and an aborted edit provides no forward state transition there.
amendFrozen106.atomicity: Simple within the existing single 105-to-106 outer transaction.
amendFrozen106.impact: Changes the raw migration bytes and statement vector, invalidates the successor manifest/compiler, 106 direct fixtures, PG15 transformer pin and all role-qualified PG17 evidence. It conflicts with the applied/frozen migration rule.
amendFrozen106.verificationCost: Full 106 source freeze, compiler, unit, PG15 dual-clean, PG17 constituent/aggregate/race classification and hosted evidence must be rebuilt; historical receipts remain historical only.

forward107.invalidStateBehavior: Require a new capability version. If 107 is absent, rolls back or remains unsealed, the updated app rejects old v1 and performs no claim/quota/provider work. Invalid ACL can be normalized by explicit canonical grants/revokes with readback or left held, but must never be silently sealed.
forward107.atomicity: One forward transaction changes the admission getter/contract to held and preserves existing release receipts and OCR results; a separately bound compiler seals only after the 107 ledger and exact allowlist match.
forward107.impact: Preserves all 106 hashes and evidence. Adds a 107 migration, manifest/compiler transition, versioned app preflight, direct SQL fixtures and a separately pinned PG15 replay adapter.
forward107.verificationCost: Incremental new 107 unit/SQL/PG15/PG17/hosted gates. Higher code count than editing 106, but lower custody risk and valid for already-applied 106 state.

structureComparison.recommendation: Use a forward 107 with a versioned fail-closed capability. Do not rewrite 106. Keep the release state machine and receipt data unchanged; scope 107 to independent canonical ACL/owner admission and ledger-bound readback.
